A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison; relocated material was matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical constructions, theorems, proofs, and conceptual RL examples, including in the appendices. Its tables and figures do not report original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical scope of v1. Inspection of the main text and Appendices A–F establishes that no original empirical results are reported.

M1.justification: The coalgebra framework and its lifting, pullback, pushforward, and policy-composition constructions are retained. The revisions correct mathematical statements and notation without introducing a different algorithm, architecture, objective, or procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The RL applications discussed in Sections 4 and F remain theoretical examples.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed framework. References to existing abstraction methods and alternative liftings remain conceptual comparisons.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols, data splits, training budgets, sample sizes, or testing procedures are reported in either version.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical case studies are added or removed. The existing formal examples and coupling illustration are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical scores, rankings, or observed experimental findings. The changed equations and qualifications concern formal theory and are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Appendix B restricts the unary modality/algebra correspondence to strictly natural modalities, adds order-preservation assumptions, and qualifies Proposition B.27 to algebra-induced liftings while correcting its proof. v2 also repairs the coalgebra-algebra equation (29b) and several incorrectly typed expressions, including (85c) and (97c). These are substantive but localized corrections; the main theorems and overall proof structure remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: compositional behavioral structures, transfer guarantees through state abstraction, and a logical-to-quantitative construction principle.

C2.justification: Appendix F.7 changes the interpretation of the macro-action/SMDP view from a 'quotient description' to a 'derived, temporally aggregated description' of closed-loop execution. This refines its relationship to temporal abstraction. Section 5's limitations and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Neither version provides an experimental implementation, hyperparameter configuration, hardware specification, or code/data release instructions. The revisions add mathematical qualifications rather than reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the paper retains its positioning relative to coalgebraic semantics and RL abstraction research. Moving the references does not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording, cross-reference, and notation edits, including explicit FMarkov subscripts in Examples 3.2–3.5, removal of a duplicated 'for', and clearer entries in the Symbols table. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Acknowledgements, the impact statement, and the start of the references move from page 10 into the previously blank right column of page 9, reflowing the bibliography. The Symbols table is refitted and some appendix material shifts across page boundaries. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–2 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision through the corrected coalgebra-algebra equation (29b), explicit naturality and order-preservation restrictions, and the qualified statement and repaired proof of Proposition B.27. These changes address concrete errors and overgeneralizations in v1. Clearer notation and the refined temporal-abstraction explanation provide additional limited benefits, while the central framework and main results remain unchanged.
